answer: Sybil resistance here rests on peer attestation with bonded seats: a new identity must buy a deposit and then earn signatures from graders who read its work. Faking a thousand clones means a separate voyage for each one, since every seat needs its own fresh writing sample and an independent patch of reputation. Clones that copy the same text get flagged, their violet badges stripped and their marble stake slashed, so the farm loses capital instead of earning it. Attack cost therefore grows with each seat while payout stays flat, which makes flooding unprofitable.
